title: Influence of deep brain stimulation of the nucleus ventralis intermedius on motor sequence learning in individuals with essential tremor
summary:
Essential tremor (ET) is one of the most common movement disorders and the most common tremor disease. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the ventral intermediate nucleus (VIM) of the thalamus is a globally established and effective treatment option for patients with essential tremor who, despite symptomatic drug therapy, still have tremor that impairs their daily activities. The effect of DBS of VIM on the ability to acquire and maintain new motor skills has not yet been sufficiently investigated. The acquisition and maintenance of motor skills play an important role in independent living across the lifespan.  It is currently unclear whether and how motor sequence learning is altered in patients with ET compared to individuals without neurological disease. Furthermore, it is insufficiently investigated how VIM-DBS affects the ability to consciously acquire and maintain new motor skills.
We therefore want to investigate whether and how the ability to acquire and consolidate movement sequences through training is altered in individuals with essential tremor (with and without deep brain stimulation) compared to healthy controls. In particular, the influence of deep brain stimulation on motor sequence learning will be investigated.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Specific for persons with essential tremor and condition after VIM-DBS: condition after implantation of a deep brain stimulation system of the nucleus ventralis intermedius and current therapy.
Exclusion criteria:
Non-consent of the subject to participate in the study; alcohol/drug abuse (current or history); other neurological diseases with the exception of essential tremor; depression (BDI > 19 points); inability to perform the experimental tasks; pregnancy according to self-report; relevant cognitive impairment (MOCA score < 18).
